note: Practical task for the Level 2 Mould Remediation pilot (GP-658). Instructor-graded against the rubric. SME review required before it is published.

assessment.title: Level 2 Mould Remediation — Practical task: plan and evidence a bathroom job
assessment.instructions:
## Practical task

Plan a Level 2 mould remediation for a real bathroom or laundry job you have worked on, or use the supplied job: a 2.4 m × 1.8 m bathroom in Hobart with growth on the back of the plasterboard behind the vanity (estimated 1.4 m²) after a slow leak from the shower recess, now fixed. The home was built in 1996. A 70-year-old occupant with a lung condition lives there.

Submit one PDF or a set of photos and documents containing:

1. **First look and moisture map.** A sketch of the room with numbered reading points, readings, a dry reference and the drying goal. Photos with a tape measure in shot if you use a real job.
2. **Stop-and-escalate check.** Each trigger from the card, answered yes or no, with a reason.
3. **Scope.** Area in m², containment type and size in m³, air scrubber choice with the air-change calculation, removal and cut lines, cleaning method, drying goal and equipment, verification and waste, in work order.
4. **SWMS summary.** Hazards and controls from the top of the hierarchy down, including respiratory protection and fit testing.
5. **Occupant plan.** How the occupant is protected during the work, and what you will say to them, in plain English.
6. **Handover note.** What was found, what will be removed and why, how it will be verified, and what the occupant must do to keep it dry.

Use Australian English, metric units and 230 V equipment throughout. Do not copy text from any standard.

criteria.label: Moisture map and dry reference
criteria.description: Numbered points, readings against a stated dry reference on the same material, and a drying goal set from it.

criteria.label: Stop-and-escalate checks
criteria.description: Every trigger answered with a reason. The 1996 build is before 2003, so asbestos is treated as possible: the plan stops before any cutting until suspect material is identified by a competent or licensed person. The vulnerable occupant is recognised and changes the plan. Because the occupant has a lung condition, the learner recommends that an independent assessor assesses the home before work starts.

criteria.label: Scope in work order and metric
criteria.description: Area in m², containment in m³, removal, cleaning, drying, verification and waste, in the order the work happens, with any Condition 2 assumption and its reasons stated.

criteria.label: Negative air calculation
criteria.description: Volume × air changes (at least 4 per hour) ÷ real (derated) airflow, with the exhaust point, a manometer log against −5 Pa, a smoke-test plan and a stop-work rule for a breach.

criteria.label: Controls and respiratory protection
criteria.description: Hierarchy of controls applied from the top down; respirator type stated and justified for removal above about 1 m² (a PAPR, or P3 with full face or hood), with fit testing and the doffing order.

criteria.label: Occupant communication and handover
criteria.description: Plain-English explanation, GP referral for health questions, and clear steps for the occupant to keep the area dry.

criteria.label: Australian production and licence
criteria.description: Australian English, metric units and 230 V equipment; standards named only, no copied standard text.
